content: Women's College Hospital, also known as The New Women's College Hospital, is a teaching hospital located in downtown Toronto. This institution is dedicated to advancing women's health, conducting research in women's health, and providing ambulatory care services. It holds the unique distinction of being the only collaborating centre in the Western Hemisphere designated by the World Health Organization. The hospital was originally established on October 1, 1883, under the name Women's Medical College. It was the first medical school in Toronto to admit women as students. Today, it operates as an independent ambulatory care hospital. In 1935, the hospital relocated to its current site in Toronto, and in 1961, it became a teaching hospital affiliated with the University of Toronto. In 1998, Women's College Hospital merged with Sunnybrook Hospital and the Orthopedic and Arthritic Hospital under the provisions of Ontario Bill 51, forming the Sunnybrook and Women's College Health Sciences Centre. However, in 2006, the hospital de-amalgamated and re-established itself as The New Women's College Hospital. In 2003, while still part of the Sunnybrook and Women's College Health Sciences Centre, the Women's College site became home to Canada's first ambulatory SARS clinic. Concurrently, the Sunnybrook site housed both the first in-patient SARS unit and the Intensive Care Unit for SARS in Canada. The current Physician-in-Chief of Women's College Hospital is Dr. Gillian Hawker.
